verdict.summary: Okta's latest quarter is a cash-conversion story more than a growth story. Q2 FY27 revenue rose 11% to $805M, RPO reached $4.858B and cRPO $2.585B; free cash flow of $227M represented a 28% margin. Identity remains mission-critical, and every human, service account and autonomous agent needs authentication and lifecycle governance. Yet 11% growth does not justify a hypergrowth label, while stock compensation and past security failures remain relevant to per-share trust. The dated framework values Okta at 8.8x FY27 guided revenue with a 3.2% annualized FCF yield. A completed 15-minute close above $172.91 is required; the $166.1499 gap-open pivot is the stop. Targets of $184.59 and $193.20 are measured from the pre-gap base and August 27 range. The thesis fails on weaker cRPO conversion, margin reversal or another identity incident.

business.overview:
Okta earns subscription revenue from workforce identity and Auth0 customer identity products. Contract value grows through seats, applications, governance modules, privileged access and machine-to-machine usage; cRPO is the cleanest near-term demand measure. Workforce products secure employees and contractors, while Auth0 is embedded by developers inside customer applications.

AI agents create non-human identities that still need discovery, authentication, authorization and policy enforcement. Okta monetizes that expansion only when agent identity products attach to existing contracts and lift cRPO, not when AI appears in product names. Governance and privileged-access modules can increase spend without relying solely on workforce-seat growth.

The model breaks if Microsoft bundles identity more aggressively, customers consolidate platforms, or another security incident damages trust. Slower workforce-seat growth and weak channel execution can also keep revenue near low-double digits despite better margins. Auth0 must preserve developer loyalty while enterprise selling becomes more efficient; otherwise independent identity becomes a premium point solution competing against suite economics.
business.moat: Okta's moat is neutral connectivity across heterogeneous clouds, applications and directories, reinforced by integration breadth and identity-policy switching costs. It is weaker inside Microsoft-standardized estates, where Entra bundling can turn identity from an independent control plane into a suite feature.

earnings.beatNote: Q2 FY27 revenue was $805M (+11%), RPO $4.858B (+17%) and cRPO $2.585B (+14%). Free cash flow reached $227M, or 28% of revenue, and FY27 revenue guidance increased to $3.216B-$3.226B. GAAP profitability improved, but non-GAAP operating income and EPS exclude stock compensation, acquired-intangible amortization and other specified adjustments. The caveat is growth: backlog is healthier than revenue, yet low-double-digit expansion must persist and convert into GAAP margin for the raised outlook to justify the valuation. Okta's next earnings date is not confirmed by the primary documents used here.

capitalStructure.shareHistory: Okta's Q2 FY27 diluted weighted-average count was 178,808,000 shares. That is the minimum calculable quarterly denominator, not a point-in-time fully diluted count; the current theoretical total is unavailable because the filing does not aggregate all unvested or anti-dilutive awards. The balance sheet carries $2.59B of cash against $411M of debt, so liquidity does not require an equity raise. No prospectus supplement or ATM was reviewed. Recurring employee equity, partly offset by repurchases, remains the relevant ownership-cost channel.

filings.finding: The July-quarter 10-Q supports $2.585B cRPO, $227M free cash flow and the $2.59B cash position; liquidity is strong, while employee equity remains the principal dilution channel.

The earnings 8-K and direct Exhibit 99.1 report $805M revenue, 17% RPO growth, 14% cRPO growth and raised FY2027 revenue guidance of $3.216B-$3.226B. The security classification and funding status are stated without inference.

macro.impact: Okta sits at the identity-control layer of enterprise software. Hiring, application count and cloud migration affect human seats; autonomous agents add machine identities and policy events. A slowdown in enterprise projects hurts cRPO, while a breach can freeze purchasing across the identity category regardless of broader cyber spending.

Position sizing must respect that narrow stop, and no chase is permitted after a gap beyond the stated threshold.
